analysis.title: Multi-Asset Strategy Daily
key_insights: 10Y UST yields are back below 5% (around 4.97%) after a weak 2Y auction. The curve is flattening, with 2s10s near 1-month lows after a front-end-led sell-off. Mizuho expects quiet conditions ahead of tomorrow's FOMC but sees the belly staying under pressure near term.

The 5% level in 10Y USTs is the key level. Yesterday's failure to hold a break above it makes it near-term resistance, but Mizuho is reluctant to chase the overnight rally ahead of the Fed. Today brings a $70bn 5Y note auction as another supply test.
DXY kept rising overnight to near 102.2. EUR/USD is around 1.1160 and Mizuho keeps a bias for a weaker EUR because elevated energy prices and higher US real rates dominate.

Brent is rangebound this week at around $116pb. Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials met Iranian leaders in Tehran, partly about reopening Hormuz, but headlines point to potential attacks in Saudi Arabia. Shipping and regional security risks stay elevated, and a rising energy risk premium is justified if there is no progress.

Moody's decision not to downgrade France drove another leg of OAT outperformance. The 10Y OAT-Bund spread tightened about 12-13bp and 10Y Bund yields finished around 3.36%. Positioning could allow more OAT tightening, but Mizuho would not chase it ahead of the ECB and November supply.

Bunds are likely to trade off global rates and wait for Thursday's ECB meeting rather than react to the Bank Lending Survey or M3. Supply today is €5bn Schatz and €3.5bn Italian short-end and linker paper.

Gilts bull-flattened, with 10Y yields falling towards 5.30% and the 10Y Gilt-Bund spread near 196bp. Tomorrow's Autumn Budget is the focus, with a £4.5bn 5Y gilt auction today. The key question is whether the OBR borrowing trajectory and fiscal headroom validate the recent Gilt recovery.
October UK shop-price inflation rose to 2.1% YoY. A hike at the November MPC is almost fully priced. GBP/USD is under pressure near 1.3325.

Asian equities were mixed, with tech in South Korea and Japan leading as the AI trade continued after Anthropic's IPO filing. USD/JPY kept rising to around 157.75, and JGBs saw selling in the ultra-long end after the long-end tap auction.

sector_views.rationale: AI trade remains closely watched and performed in early Asian trading after Anthropic's IPO filing, led by tech in South Korea and Japan.

earnings_insights: Coca-Cola, HSBC and Visa report today. The report gives no estimates for them.
